candidate.answerReason: Under the ordinary thin-coating interpretation, paint use is proportional to surface area. Each small statue requires \((1/6)^2\) pint, so 540 require 15 pints.

methods.label: Scale the painted surface area
methods.explanation:
Use the usual thin-coating model: painting to the same thickness requires the same amount of paint per unit surface area. Thus we need the surface-area scale factor.

Each small statue has height \(1/6\) of the original. Because the statues are similar, every corresponding length has this same factor, so surface area has factor
\[
\left(\frac16\right)^2=\frac1{36}.
\]
Each small statue therefore needs \(1/36\) pint. For \(540\) statues, the total is
\[
540\cdot\frac1{36}=\boxed{15\text{ pints}},
\]
choice E under this paint-coverage model.
methods.levelReason: Similarity, squared surface-area scaling, and direct proportion are elementary geometry and arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task assesses the square-law surface-area factor for similar solids and its application to paint quantity. Ratio meaning identifies the length factor, and direct proportion converts surface area and object count into total paint use.
limitations: The answer retains the recorded constant-coverage, thin-coating idealization. Equal absolute thickness alone does not make exact finite-thickness coating volume obey a square law.
